correctness.rationale: All TPRDF labels are covered by exact 9-column-symbol/81-two-column-state recurrence with explicit boundary sentinels. The full 81-state min-cost shifts from lengths 3-5 to 6-8 propagate to all lengths by min-plus homogeneity. With phase-repeating optimal predecessor matrices, exact vanishing fourth state-count differences through length 17 imply all state counts are cubic-or-lower polynomials in block index. Four exact terminal values per phase determine the asserted residue formulas. Direct all-label graph enumeration independently checks lengths 2-6 and witnesses are constructed for every residue. No finite sample is substituted for induction.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2023 paper provides parameter inequalities, upper-bound equality classes and a tree classification, but not optimal multiplicities for a ladder. The 2022 theorem applies to perfect Roman domination of grids with both factors larger than five, excluding the two-row ladder and omitting total support. The 2024 abstract describes complexity and upper bounds for different invariants. None of those statements implies the present counts.

originality.rationale: The exact two-row ladder minimum and all minimum-function multiplicities do not follow from the inspected 2023 foundational results (general comparisons, NP-completeness and tree equality families), nor from the 2022 perfect Roman product bounds (different invariant, path factors both larger than five). The indexed 2024 related Cartesian-product paper concerns perfect Roman and perfect Italian domination, not the present total condition, based on its abstract. Targeted published-result and semantic comparisons located no statement equivalent to the phase-dependent formulas or stronger result implying them. This is best-knowledge originality, not a guarantee of worldwide priority.

value.rationale: The 2023 introduction and NP-completeness of total perfect Roman domination motivate exact tractable graph families. The present theorem gives a sharp infinite minimum plus the complete optimum multiplicity, revealing unique three-periodic minima when length is a multiple of three and linear/quadratic growth otherwise. These natural equality-case counts are not supplied by general bounds and provide a structural benchmark for further width and boundary-condition studies.
